summary:
The Little Blue Macaw, *Cyanopsitta spixii*, was a breathtaking cerulean bird native to the dry gallery woodlands along Brazil's rio São Francisco in Bahia. Slender and luminous, it depended on a narrow ribbon of specialized habitat that had sheltered it for millennia. By the time researchers located the last wild population in the 1980s, only three individuals remained — and all were soon captured for illegal trade.

What followed was a quiet, heartbreaking disappearance. A lone wild male survived into 2000, the last of his kind under an open sky. Centuries of habitat destruction, the illegal pet trade, an invasive bee species, and hydroelectric development had collectively erased him from the wild. He was last seen at the end of 2000, and never confirmed again.
